medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The CMU College of Medicine strives to enhance the learning environment by promoting a culture of inclusion and mutual respect. As a core value, diversity encompasses inclusiveness, mutual respect and varied perspectives, and the College of Medicine recognizes the importance of a variety of experiences and perspectives in its students, faculty and staff. We seek to carefully select future students through a holistic admissions process, considering a multitude of factors that influence students' ability to contribute to our inclusive culture. The CMU College of Medicine will utilize a comprehensive approach to recruit, select and retain a diverse group of faculty and staff. We strive to train a diverse group of physicians whose backgrounds will enhance, shape and promote healthcare for underserved populations, with a focus in central and northern Michigan in both urban and rural areas.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence (LOA) is an approved leave from the medical school for a definite period of time, not to exceed one year. A leave of absence must be approved by the Associate Dean of Student Affairs and the Associate Dean of Medical Education.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Central Michigan University provides students with opportunities to become involved in more than 240 student organizations. Students are encouraged to take part in activities of interest to them. A wide range of interests can be pursued through organizations that focus on social issues, student governance, pre-professional development, entertainment, community service, hobbies, club sports, or religion. Involvement in student organizations is an excellent way to develop leadership skills.

For more information, please click on the following link: 
https://www.cmich.edu/academics/colleges/college-of-medicine/education/md/students
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The College of Medicine is housed in a 61,000 square foot purpose-built medical education building on the campus of Central Michigan University. It is a Leadership in Energy Efficient Design (LEED) building with sustainable design features such as bamboo installation, composite floors, low Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC), and auto shut-off lighting. The medical education building includes a large auditorium, discussion rooms, small group study rooms, anatomy laboratories, resource laboratories, and a state of the art simulation laboratory and standardized patient suite. Specific space has also been designed for student lounge and student study spaces.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Central Michigan University College of Medicine students can choose from a variety of safe and affordable housing options from on-campus residence halls and apartments to off-campus rooms, apartments, and houses at both the West and East Campuses (Mt. Pleasant and Saginaw, MI).
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
Resources from both the CMU main campus and College of Medicine are available to all medical students
https://www.cmich.edu/academics/colleges/college-of-medicine/education/md/osa
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: We are committed to supporting our students through medical school with a variety of services including career counseling, financial aid counseling, academic assistance, referrals to health and counseling services, advisement of student organizations and more. See this website and the student handbook for further details. We are conveniently located on the first floor of the Covenant HealthCare College of Medicine at Central Michigan University building (room 1401), so please stop in.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Peer tutors are available to assist students who may require course-specific academic assistance. These tutors are advanced medical students and graduate students.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Large group sessions, team-based learning (TBL), laboratory sessions and small group learning (PBL).
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is not typically mandatory for lecture sessions. Attendance is usually required at small and large group instructional activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Central Michigan University College of Medicine educational program focuses on team-based education as well as on serving the needs of the community. Small group learning, early longitudinal clinical experiences and independent study are emphasized. The first two years are organized around physiological systems starting with the Foundational Sciences of Medicine which provides students with an important baseline of knowledge of variations on normal human health, wellness, and development. The subsequent organ system block courses use the clinical presentation model to provide instruction in system specific disorders and diseases.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The CMU College of Medicine has a strong commitment to provide physicians to meet the needs of underserved rural and urban populations in central and northern Michigan. The curriculum, however, prepares students to enter any medical specialty.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Research opportunities are available to medical students beginning in their first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research is encouraged and CMED offers many research opportunities.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Central Michigan University College of Medicine will prepare physicians focused on improving access to high quality health care in Michigan with an emphasis on rural and urban medically underserved regions. The College of Medicine's curriculum is designed to prepare students for practice in communities throughout central and northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula. The curriculum incorporates the health issues and concerns most prevalent in this region as the foundation for student learning of the foundational (basic) and clinical sciences. Clinical skills training begins in the first year of the curriculum and includes training in how to diagnose and care for patients in medical clinics, state-of-the-art simulations and broad technology integration throughout the learning process.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission
The Central Michigan University (CMU) College of Medicine educates diverse students and trains culturally competent physicians to provide comprehensive health care and services to underserved populations in Michigan and beyond. Our faculty, staff and graduates advance health and wellness through exceptional education, innovative research, quality patient care and strategic collaborations to improve the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.

CMU College of Medicine recruits and admits students from Michigan to care for Michigan - especially those who are committed to pursue a career in primary care and serve the medically underserved.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
CMU College of Medicine's recommendation for coursework taken during the Winter/Spring 2020 time frame:

As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, many colleges and universities have offered students a pass/fail or credit/no credit option. We want all future Central Michigan University College of Medicine applicants to know that we will allow pass/fail or credit/no credit grades for any coursework taken during the impacted time frame, including prerequisite coursework. While we believe that academic coursework is an important component of your preparation for medical school, we don’t believe that an applicant’s total body of academic preparation should be negatively impacted by the disruptions caused by the COVID-19 outbreak.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We will consider and evaluate any graduate or postbacc work included on the AMCAS application.  Applicants with undergraduate GPA's below 3.0 will need to successfully complete additional Graduate or postbacc work to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The CMU College of Medicine does accept coursework from a Community College, but highly recommends pre-requisite work and upper level science courses be taken at a four-year institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants can submit Letter of Intent/Letter of Interest/Notice of Significant Updates via the online admissions portal after receiving a secondary application invite.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The CMU College of Medicine is committed to minimizing student indebtedness. The Office of Financial Aid will provide aid awards for students that include scholarships and loans. The director of financial aid will provide counseling on financial aid issues and will assist in developing budgets for managing living and education expenses. Financial aid recipients will receive in-depth, one- on-one counseling as well as group counseling regarding information on monthly budgeting, loan disbursements, alternative loan programs, repayment options, and loan consolidation.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy:
CMU College of Medicine does not have a Guaranteed Tuition Policy

Financial Aid Refund Policy

100% refund of tuition will be issued for students who withdraw prior to the first day of classes. Once classes begin, refunds will be calculated as follows:

•	100% refund for withdrawal during the first week of the term
•	50% refund for withdrawal during the second through fourth week of the term
•	No refund will be made after the fourth week of the term

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: All admitted students who hold multiple acceptances must select 'PLAN TO ENROLL' by April 30, 2026.

CMU requires admitted applicants to select 'COMMIT TO ENROLL' on AMCAS by 5 pm EDT on July 1. Selecting 'COMMIT TO ENROLL' indicates that you have made your final selection and have withdrawn from all waitlists. Failure to comply with this protocol may result in CMU withdrawing your acceptance.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The CMU College of Medicine uses a holistic admissions process and seeks to admit students who have personal characteristics and interests that align with the CMU College of Medicine mission. The holistic review process balances the applicant's academic portfolio with other aspects of their application, such as the capacity for using critical thinking and logic, the understanding of the principles of ethics, personal values and the qualities necessary for successful development into a compassionate, skilled physician able to serve the needs of a diverse and changing population.

In addition to the competencies listed above, we encourage applicants to review the AAMC Core Competencies for Entering Medical Students for additional information. 

The admissions process is also interested in identifying applicants who will fulfill the mission of CMED, i.e. to provide healthcare to underserved populations in central and northern Michigan.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants are expected to show competency in the area of clinical exposure, shadowing experience is just one of many ways applicants can fulfill competency in this area.  Please visit our website for more information on our admission requirements.
